question: Should the fail-closed conversation identity boundary apply to existing third-party channel plugins immediately, and how should the shipped ingress API migrate without leaving an opt-out bypass?
rationale: The feature's core security guarantee conflicts with its compatibility design: the public unversioned plugin path remains unenforced, so maintainer intent is needed to define the permanent plugin API and upgrade boundary.

options.title: Enforce at public ingress
options.body: Keep the existing signature source-compatible where feasible, derive or require safe identity facts, and reserve a separately named API for genuinely trusted internal turns.

options.title: Time-bound legacy compatibility
options.body: Retain unversioned ingress temporarily only with explicit deprecation, diagnostics, a removal plan, and proof that it cannot receive untrusted shared audiences.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Do not ship fail-closed identity modes until the public plugin migration contract can uphold the same boundary across all channel ingress.

recommendation.title: Enforce at public ingress
recommendation.body: Keep the existing signature source-compatible where feasible, derive or require safe identity facts, and reserve a separately named API for genuinely trusted internal turns.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue assignment and prerequisite and feature history make this person the clearest available owner for the product and security boundary.
